CHAPTER VII
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Part One
Prevention of violence against women and children

CHAPTER XII
SANCTIONS
Article 32
In the event of violence against Women and Children, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of the Laws and Regulations.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 28
(1) The regional government carries out Guidance and Supervision by means of:
a. Coordination
b. Guidance
c. Education and Training
d. Monitoring and Evaluation
(2) The implementation of coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out among stakeholders cross-sectorally with Regional Apparatus and community organizations/institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) The implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b for women and children who become victims is carried out through guidance on religious values and social values, counseling, social rehabilitation, and social assistance by the competent Regional Apparatus together with other related agencies.
(4) The implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is provided to women and children who become victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the competent Regional Apparatus, Work Training Centers, and other related agencies.
(5) The implementation of guidance and supervision for women and children who become victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3), and paragraph (4) is carried out through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs and the interests of the local community on its own initiative based on community aspirations within the system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 2. Regional Government is the administration of government affairs by the regional government and DPRD according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration of Tanggamus Regency. 4. Regent is the Regent of Tanggamus. 5. Regional Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Tanggamus Regency. 6. Regional Apparatus abbreviated as PD is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional People's Representative Council of Tanggamus Regency in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of Tanggamus Regency. 7. Regional Planning, Development, Research and Innovation Agency hereinafter abbreviated as Bapperida is the Regional Planning, Development, Research and Innovation Agency in Tanggamus Regency. 8. Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA DALDUK and KB is the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning of Tanggamus Regency. 9. Sub-district is the working area of the sub-district head as a regional apparatus of Tanggamus regency. 10. Village or called Pekon, hereinafter referred to as village/pekon, is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage the interests of the local community, based on origins and customs that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 11. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb. 12. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the State. 13. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 15. Guardian is a parent or body that in fact exercises custody power as a parent over a child. 16. Woman is a human being who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth and breastfeed. 17. Child Marriage is a marriage conducted through civil, religious or customary law with or without registration or official consent where one or both partners are children under the age of 18 years. 18. Children in Need of Special Protection hereinafter abbreviated as AMPK are Children in need of special protection. 19. Worst Forms of Child Labor hereinafter referred to as BPTA is the worst forms of child labor. 20. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 21. Street child is a child whose life is irregular, spending most of their time outside the home to earn a living on the streets or in public places. 22. Child with disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental obstacles that interfere with their growth and development normally. 23. Gifted child is a child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 24. Child in conflict with the law is a child who conflicts with the law, a child who becomes a victim of a criminal act, and a child who becomes a witness to a criminal act. 25. Adopted Child is a Child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the Family of Parents, legal Guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education and raising of that Child into the environment of the Family of adoptive Parents based on a court decision or determination. 26. Foster Child is a Child who is cared for by a person or institution to be provided with guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health because the Parents or one of the Parents is unable to guarantee the normal growth and development of the Child. 27. Economically exploited child is an action with or without the consent of the child who becomes a victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical exploitation, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a child by another party to obtain material benefits. 28. Sexually exploited child is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of a child to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and sexual abuse. 29. Child labor is children both male and female who are involved in economic activities that interfere with or hinder the growth and development process and are dangerous to the physical and mental health of children. 30. Article 26
(1) Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
(3) Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

Article 15

(3) The form of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 6
Psychological violence as referred to in Article 4 letter b constitutes acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, social including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 39. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, and psychologically. 40. Violence Against Women and Children in the Household is any act against a woman and child that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, economically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household sphere. 41. Child Abuse is any action against a child, including placing a child in a situation that can cause adverse impacts on the welfare, safety, dignity and development of the child. 43. Assistance is social work that has professional competence in its field. 44. Child Neglect is any act of neglecting the fulfillment of basic needs, care, and maintenance that interferes with or hinders child development, including leaving a child in a dangerous situation. 45. Prevention is the effort of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect of children. 46. Risk Reduction is early action toward children and their families who are in vulnerable situations or at risk of experiencing various forms of violence, abuse, exploitation, and neglect. 47. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of children who become victims of acts of violence, abuse, exploitation, and or neglect. 48. Care Environment is care by parents and care outside parental care. PATBM is a movement of networks or citizen groups at the community level working in a coordinated manner to achieve child protection goals. 50. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD is a regional development planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years. 51. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJMD is a regional development planning document for a period of 5 (five) years. 52. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 53. Child Participation Forum / Regional child forum is an organization that accommodates the aspirations of children and/or groups of children in Tanggamus Regency. 54. Repatriation is an Effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or receiving area to the area of origin. 55. Child Social Welfare Institution is a social organization or social association that implements Child Social Welfare Administration formed by the community, whether legally incorporated or not legally incorporated. 58. Alternative care is child care carried out by Child Social Welfare Institutions. 59. Child participation is the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly carried out with the consent and will of the child based on awareness and understanding. 60.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

Article 5
Physical violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, termination/loss of pregnancy, loss of consciousness and/or causes the death of women and/or children.

Second Part
Forms and Mechanisms of Services for Violence Against Women and Children

CHAPTER XI
FUNDING
Article 30
Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD); and
b. Other legal and non-binding sources.

SCOPE
Article 3
The Scope in this Regional Regulation is as follows: a. Forms of Violence against Women and Children b. Rights of Victims of Acts of Violence Against Women and Children c. Obligations and Responsibilities
d. Protection of Women and Children
e. Cooperation, Partnership and Empowerment
f. Guidance and Supervision
g. Child-Friendly Regency (KLA) and Parahita Ekapraya Award (APE)

REGENT OF TANGGAMUS,

Law Number 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2003 Number 39, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia 4279), as has been amended several times most recently by Law Number 17 of 2016 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2016 Number 99, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia 5882); 7. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419); 9. Law Number 13 of 2006 concerning Protection of Witnesses and Victims (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2006 Number 64, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4635), as has been amended by Law Number 31 of 2014 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 293, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5602); 10. Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606); 14. Government Regulation Number 70 of 2020 Concerning Procedures for Implementation of Chemical Castration Actions, Installation of Electronic Detection Devices, Rehabilitation, and Announcement of the Identity of Perpetrators of Sexual Violence Against Children (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2020 Number 269, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 6585); 18. 6.1.rationale: In the Indonesian source, Pasal 4 huruf f angka (2) only lists “Korban bencana dan konflik” as one category under “kekerasan lainnya” (other violence). The regulation’s operative provisions on prevention (Pasal 19–20), services/UPTD PPA (Pasal 21–24), cooperation (Pasal 25–26), and funding (Pasal 30–31) are general for women/children victims of violence and do not set out specific/targeted protection measures for women in disaster/conflict/emergency/displacement contexts. Therefore the judge’s ‘No’ reasoning matches the actual content; the golden ‘Yes’ appears to be based merely on the mention of disaster/conflict victims, which is not enough to constitute a dedicated measure for this indicator.

6.3.evaluator_rationale: The policy includes a specific measure related to women in the work context by calling for the creation of a friendly and safe work environment atmosphere for women.

g. Child-Friendly Regency (KLA) and Parahita Ekapraya Award (APE)

Article 6
Psychological violence as referred to in Article 4 letter b constitutes acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

6.3.rationale: The Indonesian text explicitly includes a work-context measure for women: Pasal 19 ayat (2) huruf c states “Menciptakan suasana lingkungan kerja yang ramah dan aman bagi perempuan” (creating a friendly and safe work environment for women). This is a specific provision addressing women in the workplace (women workers) within the prevention section. Since this content is present, a ‘Yes’ is supportable; thus the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect rather than the model being wrong.

6.5.evaluator_rationale: Although “Persons with disabilities” are listed among categories of other violence, the excerpts do not describe any special protection measures targeted at women with disabilities or persons with disabilities.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs and the interests of the local community on its own initiative based on community aspirations within the system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 2. Regional Government is the administration of government affairs by the regional government and DPRD according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration of Tanggamus Regency. 4. Regent is the Regent of Tanggamus. 5. Regional Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Tanggamus Regency. 6. Regional Apparatus abbreviated as PD is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional People's Representative Council of Tanggamus Regency in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of Tanggamus Regency. 7. Regional Planning, Development, Research and Innovation Agency hereinafter abbreviated as Bapperida is the Regional Planning, Development, Research and Innovation Agency in Tanggamus Regency. 8. Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA DALDUK and KB is the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning of Tanggamus Regency. 9. Sub-district is the working area of the sub-district head as a regional apparatus of Tanggamus regency. 10. Village or called Pekon, hereinafter referred to as village/pekon, is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage the interests of the local community, based on origins and customs that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 11. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb. 12. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the State. 13. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 15. Guardian is a parent or body that in fact exercises custody power as a parent over a child. 16. Woman is a human being who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth and breastfeed. 17. Child Marriage is a marriage conducted through civil, religious or customary law with or without registration or official consent where one or both partners are children under the age of 18 years. 18. Children in Need of Special Protection hereinafter abbreviated as AMPK are Children in need of special protection. 19. Worst Forms of Child Labor hereinafter referred to as BPTA is the worst forms of child labor. 20. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 21. Street child is a child whose life is irregular, spending most of their time outside the home to earn a living on the streets or in public places. 22. Child with disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental obstacles that interfere with their growth and development normally. 23. Gifted child is a child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 24. Child in conflict with the law is a child who conflicts with the law, a child who becomes a victim of a criminal act, and a child who becomes a witness to a criminal act. 25. Adopted Child is a Child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the Family of Parents, legal Guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education and raising of that Child into the environment of the Family of adoptive Parents based on a court decision or determination. 26. Foster Child is a Child who is cared for by a person or institution to be provided with guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health because the Parents or one of the Parents is unable to guarantee the normal growth and development of the Child. 27. Economically exploited child is an action with or without the consent of the child who becomes a victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical exploitation, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a child by another party to obtain material benefits. 28. Sexually exploited child is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of a child to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and sexual abuse. 29. Child labor is children both male and female who are involved in economic activities that interfere with or hinder the growth and development process and are dangerous to the physical and mental health of children. 30. Custody is the power of Parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect and develop Children in accordance with their religion and in accordance with their abilities, talents, and interests. 31. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government and regional government. 32.

Article 5
Physical violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, termination/loss of pregnancy, loss of consciousness and/or causes the death of women and/or children.

CHAPTER VII
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Part One
Prevention of violence against women and children

Article 24
The provision of services to victims is carried out with principles, among others: no fees charged, fast, safe, empathy, non-discriminatory, easily accessible and confidentiality.

REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES
TANGGAMUS REGENCY
REGENT OF TANGGAMUS
DECIDES :
To Establish : REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 16
The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 13 letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect women and children as members of the family.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 28
(1) The regional government carries out Guidance and Supervision by means of:
a. Coordination
b. Guidance
c. Education and Training
d. Monitoring and Evaluation
(2) The implementation of coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out among stakeholders cross-sectorally with Regional Apparatus and community organizations/institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) The implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b for women and children who become victims is carried out through guidance on religious values and social values, counseling, social rehabilitation, and social assistance by the competent Regional Apparatus together with other related agencies.
(4) The implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is provided to women and children who become victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the competent Regional Apparatus, Work Training Centers, and other related agencies.
(5) The implementation of guidance and supervision for women and children who become victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3), and paragraph (4) is carried out through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

Article 15
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and the community as referred to in Article 13 letter b and letter c, shall be implemented in the form of participation of the private sector and the community.
(2) The form of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
 a. Preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
 b. Providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the authorized parties; and
 c. Participating in the handling of victims of violence.
(3) The form of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 6
Psychological violence as referred to in Article 4 letter b constitutes acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

Article 32

Article 10
(1) Other violence as referred to in Article 4 letter f constitutes threat of violence and coercion.
(2) Threat of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether or not using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(3) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 8
Neglect as referred to in Article 4 letter d includes: a. Acts of deliberately neglecting a woman within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obligated to provide livelihood and care to said woman.
b. Acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs in a proper manner, whether physical, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for his/her care.
c. Acts of deliberately neglecting to care for or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for his/her care.

6.5.rationale: In the Indonesian source, “Kaum disabilitas dan/ atau” appears only as a listed category under Pasal 4 huruf f angka (9) within “kekerasan lainnya” (other violence). The regulation does not provide specific protections, accommodations, or tailored service provisions for persons/women with disabilities beyond general victim services and general principles (e.g., Pasal 21–24, including ‘non diskriminatif’ in Pasal 24). Merely listing disability as a category is not the same as setting out targeted measures for people with disabilities. The judge’s ‘No’ is consistent with the text; the golden ‘Yes’ likely over-credited the mention in the list.
